clue.text: Talk repeatedly about something to sit on

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the two words for talk are each read backwards in place

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
the second word for talk, gab, is idle chatter too

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going on and on about a chair or cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns GAS and GAB, two words for talk ('repeatedly' calls for a second one), giving SAG and BAG. A sag bag is a bean bag; the grid's RAGBAG is a slip, its first letter being unchecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A sag bag is a floppy bean-filled seat, so it is a piece of furniture you sit on.

clue.text: Dance mother joins in completely finished? Not quite

indicators.note: mother joins in, so her letters go inside the phrase for finished
not quite means the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: all ended means completely finished
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Is a dance over? Mother arrives as it is almost done.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL ENDED cut short by 'Not quite' is ALLENDE, and 'joins in' puts MA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An allemande is a stately German court dance, later a movement in baroque suites.

clue.text: Attack aim of anger management course?

definitions.meaning: a heavy bombardment, an onslaught of fire
read as two words, such a course wants to ..., keep fury out

explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a concentrated bombardment; the joke splits it into bar (prohibit) and rage (fury).

clue.text: Be very keen to bypass committee?

definitions.meaning: to be excessively enthusiastic about something
taken literally, to go over the board's heads, skipping that committee

explanation.definitionFit: To go overboard is an idiom for excessive enthusiasm; read literally it means going over a board, a governing committee.

clue.text: Crime Inland Revenue cracks fast

indicators.note: cracks means breaks into, so the revenue letters go inside the word for fast

parts.note: pacy means fast
IR is the abbreviation for the former UK tax authority, the Inland Revenue

explanation.surface: A quick crime has the tax inspectors breaking into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy is robbery at sea, or copying protected work illegally: either way an offence.

clue.text: Fool around in part of 2?

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word for fool is read backwards

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: Someone is messing about during a piece of the second clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is ALLEMANDE, a dance, and a pas is a step in a dance, so it is part of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas is a single step in ballet or other dance, one element of a dance.

clue.text: Theatre company wants wage increase for extra performance

parts.note: rep is short for repertory, a theatre company
a rise is a pay increase in British English

explanation.surface: A theatre company asks for a pay rise in return for putting on another show.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprise is a repeat performance of a piece, such as a song sung again later in a show.

clue.text: British actor going on and on? Not half

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of the word for going on and on is kept

parts.note: continuous means going on without a break

explanation.surface: A British actor who never stops talking, or perhaps only half does.
explanation.walkthrough: CONTINUOUS loses its second half, NUOUS, to 'Not half'. Tom Conti is a Scottish stage and film actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Conti is a well-known Scottish-born actor, star of Shirley Valentine.

clue.text: Make changes to official order Conservative ignored

indicators.note: ignored means left out, so the letter for Conservative is dropped from the word

parts.note: an edict is an official decree

explanation.surface: A politician revises an official order the Tories have disregarded.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to revise or alter text, so it means altering.

clue.text: Playwright, a desperate fellow after drink, say

indicators.note: after places the fellow's name behind the drink
say signals a word spoken, so the drink's sound gives the first part

parts.note: sherry is a fortified wine
Desperate Dan is the strongman of the British children's comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A dramatist resembles a hopeless man who has been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: SHERI sounds like sherry. Desperate Dan is a British comic-strip character, so 'a desperate fellow' is a Dan.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan was an Irish dramatist who wrote The Rivals and The School for Scandal.

clue.text: Wild one taken back to the States via S American port

indicators.note: back means the words for one and taken are read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
led means taken somewhere, as a guide takes someone
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port, is Rio for short
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A wild person is brought back to America through a South American harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns only the first two pieces, giving DELI; 'taken' is the past tense of lead here, not seized.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirious means frenzied or raving, in a state of uncontrolled excitement.

clue.text: Hit magazine, now defunct

definitions.meaning: the British humorous weekly that closed in 2002

explanation.definitionFit: A punch is a blow with the fist; Punch was also the long-running British satirical weekly, now closed.

clue.text: French dish with German rolls and British beer

indicators.note: rolls means turned over, so the German word is read backwards

parts.note: mit is the German word for with
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A French meal served alongside German bread rolls and British ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' turns MIT, German for with, into TIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbale is a French dish of minced ingredients baked in a drum-shaped mould.

clue.text: Maybe Top of the Pops is back with Queen louder than before?

parts.note: the top record in the charts is number one, written NO 1

indicators.note: back means the little word is is read in reverse

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen

explanation.surface: Is the chart show back with Queen, and making more noise than it used to?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe Top of the Pops' is a number one hit, NO 1, with 1 as I. Top of the Pops was the BBC's weekly chart music show.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisier is the comparative of noisy, making more din than previously.

clue.text: Food in home turns bad

indicators.note: bad signals the letters are spoiled, so they go into a new order

explanation.surface: Food left in the house goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges the eleven letters of IN HOME TURNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishment is the sustenance obtained from what you eat.

clue.text: Observe adults getting excited about a French film classic

indicators.note: about means the anagram letters go round the French word
getting excited signals the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: un is French for a

explanation.surface: Watch the grown-ups get worked up over a French film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the anagram (from 'getting excited') around the French article; 'film classic' is the definition, not 'French film'.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Wilder's 1950 film about a faded silent star is one of Hollywood's acknowledged masterpieces.

clue.text: Set up interest-free banking system to provide cover

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: something drab is free of interest, dull
BACS is the UK automated bank payment system

explanation.surface: Someone establishes a bank that charges no interest to give financial protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest-free' means dull, not loan-free. 'Set up' turns DRAB BACS into the answer; BACS is Britain's bank-to-bank payments system.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is a sheath for a sword, a protective casing for the blade.

clue.text: They may be carrying drugs when stopped by police chief

indicators.note: the word for when is plugged by the police chief, who goes inside it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I arrived
a CID head leads the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK detective branch

explanation.surface: People suspected of smuggling narcotics are halted by a senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying drugs' suggests smugglers, but these people are carrying them inside, having taken LSD.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidheads are habitual users of LSD, so they have the drug in their systems.

clue.text: Western production reshown in Astoria cinema

indicators.note: reshown suggests the letters are shown again in a different order

explanation.surface: A cowboy picture is screened again at the Astoria picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' suggests a cowboy film, but the answer is the making of a place more like the USA, the West.
explanation.definitionFit: Americanisation is the process of making a culture conform to US ways, something the West produces.

clue.text: Beset by trouble, I call emergency, having nothing to lose

parts.note: to name is to call someone something

indicators.note: having nothing to lose means the zero is dropped from the distress call

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: In difficulty, I ring for help with nothing left to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: SOS loses its O to 'to lose' and becomes SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a mess means being in a muddled, difficult situation.

clue.text: A notion developed by Italian fellow

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: An Italian man comes up with an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is a common Italian man's name, as in The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Bob Dylan performing without live group

indicators.note: performing signals the singer's name is reworked into another arrangement

parts.note: L stands for live, as marked on the live terminal of an electric plug

explanation.surface: Bob Dylan on stage without an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes L (live) from the letters of BOB DYLAN, and 'performing' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy band is a pop group of young male singers.

clue.text: Juvenile hiding in dingy outhouse

indicators.note: hiding in says the answer is tucked inside the following words

explanation.surface: A youngster lurks in a grimy garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person, someone not yet adult.

clue.text: Married man had to suppress restless urge

indicators.note: to suppress means to hold down, so the urge is held inside the contraction

parts.note: he'd is short for he had
an itch is a restless craving

explanation.surface: A married man had to keep a restless desire in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to suppress' puts the urge inside the contraction; 'Married man' looks like one phrase but 'man had' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To get hitched is slang for to wed, so hitched means wed.

clue.text: Flood defence English youngster climbed

indicators.note: climbed in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: An English child scrambles up a sea wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbed' turns E KID upwards, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dike is an embankment built to hold back the sea or a river.

clue.text: Recycle rubbish fellow's thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out means the fellow's letter is removed

parts.note: refuse is rubbish
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: Someone recycles the rubbish a man has thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: To reuse something is to use it again, the point of recycling.

clue.text: Dollar note and a cent pocketed by European

indicators.note: pocketed by means held inside the word for European

parts.note: a Greek is a European
NB, nota bene, means note well

explanation.surface: A man from Europe pockets a dollar bill and a cent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' wants to join 'Dollar' as the definition; it is NB, nota bene.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenback is American slang for a dollar, from the green ink on the back of US banknotes.

clue.text: Information little girl communicated orally

indicators.note: communicated orally signals the girl's name as heard

parts.note: Jen is a short form of the name Jennifer

explanation.surface: A small girl passed on the news by word of mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Gen is British slang for the facts or the lowdown, from general information.

clue.text: Fancy one's companion being first to be picked

indicators.note: being first puts the companion ahead of the rearranged letters

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: fancy here means fancifully rearranged, signalling a new order of letters

explanation.surface: Someone's partner is the first choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb meaning desire; it rearranges ONE'S. CH is the Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Chosen means selected, singled out from others.

clue.text: Follower of eastern philosophy is absorbed by odd parts of that holy book

indicators.note: odd parts of means the first and third letters of that
absorbed by means taken inside the abbreviation for the holy book

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A disciple of Eastern thought is engrossed in strange passages of a sacred text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd parts' suggests weird passages but means the odd-numbered letters of 'that', T and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taoist practises Taoism, the Chinese philosophy of the Way.
